recommendation.thresholdSummary: Critical threshold crossed: Flash Flood Warning covering the access routes, about 14 in of water on a critical route
recommendation.explanation: 3.4 in of rain fell overnight and a Flash Flood Warning covers downtown Kansas City until 10 AM. Southwest Boulevard along Turkey Creek, one of the office's two main access routes, is closed with about 14 in of water, and several underpasses are flooded. Another 0.5 to 1 in of rain is forecast through 9 AM, so water won't recede before the morning commute. Close the office: telework-ready employees can work remotely, and no one should drive through flooded roads.
recommendation.whatCouldChange: Rain ending before 6 AM, the warning being cancelled, and routes reopening by 9 AM would support a delayed arrival. Water entering the building would keep it closed.

alerts.headline: Flash flooding is ongoing. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen, with another inch possible. Turn around, don't drown when you reach flooded roads.
Additional heavy rain may cause creeks and streams to rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings and urban underpasses are most at risk.

forecast.shortForecast: Rain ending by 10 AM, then cloudy

roads.detail: Southwest Boulevard along Turkey Creek is closed with about 14 in of water, and several downtown underpasses are flooded. Avoid low-lying routes until water recedes.
